title: Why Theo's Mattress Money Is Shrinking 😂
description:
Theo keeps $10,000 in his mattress because cash "can never lose value". Nora has bad news: the number stays the same, but what it buys doesn't.

US prices rose 3.7% over the last 12 months, so today's $10,000 only buys what $9,643 bought a year ago. If prices kept rising 3% a year, in ten years that same $10,000 would buy what $7,441 buys today. That's about $2,559 of buying power gone without a sound.

Cash keeps its number, not its power.

Where does your cash sleep: mattress, bank or invested? Tell us in the comments 👇

Follow for more numbers that change how you spend.

⚠️ Illustration only: $10,000 held as cash earning 0%. The 10-year example assumes a steady 3% inflation rate a year; real inflation changes every year. Last-year figure: US CPI-U all items +3.7% for the 12 months ending September 2026 (Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, CPI news release, 14 Oct 2026). Ignores interest, taxes and other risks. This is not financial advice.
